summary: San Rafael (Cerro Negro) Lookout in Cherry Canyon Park: 1934 county cab on a 30-ft K-brace tower, handed to Glendale for radio use in 1960; now a fenced, non-public communications site.

facts.design: Standard L-4 14x14 cab (the Register says it appears to be standard) on a 30-foot steel K-brace tower; exterior paneling and asphalt roofing added; Chrysler Victory air raid siren on a short steel tower nearby

access.note: Fenced working communications facility; the Register says it is not open to the public. Trails in Cherry Canyon Park may reach the area.

visit.trail_note: The Register says the site is fenced and not open to the public. Trails in Cherry Canyon Park may lead near it.

facts.agency: City of La Canada Flintridge (built for the Los Angeles County Fire Department)

events.note: Constructed for the Los Angeles County Fire Department in 1934; a November 1934 item says a new lookout was under construction on San Rafael peak to replace a temporary station
County annual report: fence installed to protect radio equipment, and a power line extended to the site for the radio apparatus and domestic use

Register says the county turned the lookout over to the Glendale City Fire Department for use as a communications site; a December 1960 item describes a county license for Glendale to install a radio receiver on the county-owned site, with a Civil Defense siren to remain operable
Date registered on the National Historic Lookout Register: June 28, 2017

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register says the county turned the lookout over to the Glendale City Fire Department. A December 1960 newspaper item, quoting a county supervisor, describes a license for Glendale to use the county-owned site, with county and federal control kept over the siren. The story gives both accounts and uses the newspaper's wording as the more specific one.

notes_for_editor: No fire history and no staffing details appear in either source read, so the record has no staffed or fire events. Access 'unknown' is replaced with closed, based on the Register's 'not open to the public'; that note is undated, so the present-tense access claim rests on it alone. Search snippets from AllTrails, Komoot, Yelp, Tripadvisor and Facebook describe visiting the area; they were not read and are not used. The 1945 fence and 1960 handover are added beyond the brief's two events. The 1934 build date in the brief matches the Register. The Register's 1934 photo (Pasadena Post) and 2017 photo (Brad Eells) have no license stated, so none are listed. The 30-foot height is from the Register, converted to 9.1 m. The Register lists the site under the second URL form (nhlr.org/nhlr.org/...) in the brief; it was not read separately.
